components.name: resource-url
components.description: Scheme, bucket or access-point host, and object key path; the object address is not documented as a secret.

components.name: signing-parameters
components.description: Query parameters X-Amz-Algorithm, X-Amz-Credential, X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-SignedHeaders, X-Amz-Signature, URI-encoded; X-Amz-Security-Token when temporary credentials are used. The signature is lowercase hexadecimal.

claims.statement: AWS states that presigned URLs are bearer tokens that grant access to those who possess them, limited by the permissions of the principal that created them.

sources.supports: In essence, presigned URLs are bearer tokens that grant access to those who possess them.

claims.statement: A presigned URL remains valid for the period specified when generated (up to 7 days with the AWS CLI or SDKs, 1 minute to 12 hours from the console), can be used multiple times until expiry, and expires early when the creating temporary credential expires or is revoked; expiry is checked at request time.

sources.supports: A presigned URL remains valid for the period of time specified when the URL is generated; You can use the presigned URL multiple times, up to the expiration date and time.

claims.statement: The SigV4 query-string form carries X-Amz-Algorithm, X-Amz-Credential (access key ID and credential scope), X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-SignedHeaders and X-Amz-Signature (lowercase hexadecimal); X-Amz-Security-Token holds the session token when temporary credentials are used. The documented query example is for an EC2 API request; the S3 presigned-URL page names X-Amz-SignedHeaders but does not list the whole parameter set.

sources.supports: Example: Request with authentication parameters in the query string (X-Amz-Algorithm, X-Amz-Credential, X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-SignedHeaders, X-Amz-Signature); X-Amz-Security-Token may be included in the query string.
X-Amz-SignedHeaders is named in the presigned-URL FAQ.

claims.statement: SigV4 specifies that query names and values are URI-encoded with uppercase hexadecimal escapes, unreserved characters left unencoded and space as %20, and the canonical query string sorts parameters after encoding. This governs signing, not how a URL may be written when shared.

sources.supports: UriEncode() rules: Letters in the hexadecimal value must be uppercase; sort the parameters in the canonical query string alphabetically by key name.

claims.statement: The pages call the whole presigned URL a bearer token. They do not say whether the X-Amz-Signature value alone, the query string or the whole URL is the minimal span to mask, whether X-Amz-Credential (access key ID plus scope) is public metadata, or how duplicate or reordered parameters behave in a shared URL.

sources.supports: Bearer-token statement only; no minimal-span statement.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Minimal masking extent (signature value, query string, whole URL) is not stated by AWS.
Whether duplicate or reordered X-Amz-* parameters are accepted by S3 is not documented on the pages read.
Whether an expired presigned URL is still a value to protect is a policy question, not a provider statement.
